Press firmly through the left dumbbell and row the right dumbbell up toward your right hip, driving the right elbow toward the ceiling while keeping your hips and shoulders perfectly square to the floor. Lower the right dumbbell softly to the floor, stabilize, and repeat with the left dumbbell, maintaining a rock-solid plank throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Pullover
exercises.instructions_en: Stand facing a high cable pulley with a straight-bar or rope attachment. Grasp the attachment with an overhand grip spaced shoulder-width apart. Take a step back, bend your knees slightly, and hinge forward at your hips about 30 degrees with a flat back, arms extended overhead with a slight soft micro-bend in the elbows. Keeping your arms rigid at that slight bend, pull the bar down in a wide arcing sweep toward your thighs, using pure lat contraction. Pull until the bar touches your thighs, squeeze your lats hard for a moment, then allow the cable to slowly pull your arms back up along the same wide arc to the overhead stretch position.

exercises.name: Cable High Row
exercises.instructions_en: Set the pulleys of a cable machine to high head height with dual handles or attach a wide bar to a high cable stack. Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and take a step back with knees slightly bent and core braced. With chest proud, pull the handles down and back toward your collarbones and upper chest, flaring your elbows wide out to the sides at roughly 70 to 80 degrees from your torso. Squeeze your rear deltoids, rhomboids, and middle trapezius firmly at peak contraction, then slowly return your arms forward under control to the full stretch.

exercises.name: Superman
exercises.instructions_en: Lie prone on your stomach on an exercise mat with legs straight and arms extended fully forward overhead, palms facing downward. Simultaneously engage your glutes, hamstrings, and lower back to lift your arms, chest, and thighs several inches off the floor. Keep your neck in a neutral alignment looking down toward the mat. Hold the lifted arch position for a 2-second isometric contraction, then gently lower your limbs and chest back to the starting prone position.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raises
exercises.instructions_en:
Lie face down on a mat with your forehead resting lightly down to keep the neck neutral. Extend your arms overhead at a 45-degree angle in a Y-shape with thumbs pointed toward the ceiling. Squeeze your shoulder blades together to lift your arms and upper chest off the floor, holding for a second before lowering. Next, bring arms directly out to the sides into a T-shape, lifting thumbs up. Finally, bend your elbows into your ribs forming a W-shape, retracting the scaps hard before lowering back to the mat.


=== Core ===

exercises.name: Dumbbell Side Bend
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart holding a dumbbell in your right hand at your side with palm facing inward, placing your left hand lightly behind your head or resting on your left hip. Keep your shoulders back, chest proud, and hips squared forward. Slowly bend your torso laterally to the right side, lowering the dumbbell down along the outside of your right leg toward your knee while keeping your hips stationary. Once you feel a deep stretch along your left obliques, forcefully contract your left obliques to pull your torso back upright to the vertical center, continuing slightly past center for a full contraction, then lower under control.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchopper
exercises.instructions_en: Set the cable pulley to its highest position with a single D-handle attached. Stand sideways to the cable stack, about an arm's length away, with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Grasp the handle with both hands, extending your arms diagonally up toward the pulley with a soft elbow bend. Rotate your torso and pull the cable diagonally downward across your body toward your opposite outside knee, pivoting on your rear foot and engaging your obliques. Pause at the bottom of the chop with core braced, then slowly control the resistance back along the diagonal trajectory to the starting high position.

exercises.name: Cable Seated Twist
exercises.instructions_en: Place a flat gym bench perpendicular to a cable pulley adjusted to chest height with a single D-handle. Sit tall on the bench with feet planted flat for stability. Grasp the handle with both hands and extend your arms straight out in front of your chest. Maintaining an upright spine and keeping your arms aligned with your sternum, engage your obliques to rotate your upper torso 90 degrees away from the cable stack in a smooth horizontal arc. Hold the peak rotational contraction for a moment, then slowly resist the cable tension to return to the starting position facing forward.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.instructions_en: Attach a single D-handle to a cable pulley adjusted to chest height. Stand perpendicular to the cable machine with feet shoulder-width apart in an athletic stance with soft knees. Hold the handle with both hands pressed against the center of your chest, taking a couple of steps away to create cable tension. Brace your core and glutes. Press both hands straight out in front of your chest until your arms are fully extended, resisting the rotational force trying to pull your torso toward the machine. Hold the full lockout for a two-second pause, then draw your hands slowly back to your sternum.

exercises.name: Machine Crunch
exercises.instructions_en: Sit in an abdominal crunch machine, adjusting the seat height so the machine's axis of rotation aligns with your lower ribs/lumbar spine. Hook your shins or feet comfortably under the lower ankle pads and grasp the overhead handles beside your head, resting your upper chest against the padded roller. Inhale, then exhale as you contract your abdominals to curl your upper body forward and downward, rounding your spine and bringing your ribcage toward your pelvis against the machine resistance. Squeeze your abs hard at maximum flexion, then slowly return to the upright starting position.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Windmill
exercises.instructions_en: Stand with feet positioned wider than shoulder-width apart, turning both feet 45 degrees to the left. Clean and press a kettlebell overhead with your right arm, locking your elbow with wrist straight and gazing up at the bell. Keeping your right arm locked vertically throughout, hinge your hips backward and to the right while sliding your left hand down along the inside of your left leg toward the floor. Descend until your left fingertips touch the floor or your ankle with torso rotated open, pause, then drive through your hips to return upright to the tall standing position.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Crunch
exercises.instructions_en: Lie flat on your back on a mat with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Place your fingertips lightly behind your head with elbows flared wide. Inhale, then exhale as you contract your abdominals, lifting your right shoulder blade off the floor and rotating your torso diagonally to drive your right elbow toward your left knee as your left knee simultaneously pulls inward toward your chest. Squeeze your obliques firmly as the elbow and knee approach each other, then lower your shoulder and foot smoothly back down to the mat before repeating on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Jackknife Sit-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Lie completely flat on your back on an exercise mat with legs straight, ankles together, and arms extended overhead on the floor. Inhale, brace your core, and simultaneously lift your straight legs and upper torso off the floor in a synchronized explosive motion, pivoting on your sit bones to create a sharp V-shape with your body. Reach your hands forward toward your toes or shins at the peak of the movement, pausing for a split-second balance on your glutes, then slowly lower your torso and straight legs back down under strict control to hover just above the mat.

exercises.name: Alternate Heel Touches
exercises.instructions_en: Lie supine on a mat with knees bent and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, placed a few inches from your glutes. Curl your head, neck, and shoulder blades slightly off the floor into a constant isometric crunch with arms extended straight along your sides, palms facing inward. Contract your right oblique to laterally bend your torso to the right, sliding your right fingertips to touch your right heel. Fluidly reverse direction, sliding back through center to contract your left oblique and touch your left heel with your left fingertips, maintaining steady breathing and continuous core tension.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
exercises.instructions_en: Step into a captain's chair station, resting your forearms flat on the padded arm supports and gripping the handles firmly. Press your back flat against the lumbar support pad and let your legs hang straight down with ankles together. Inhale and brace your core. Keeping your legs straight (or with a slight micro-bend) and toes pointed, contract your lower abdominals to lift your legs straight up in front of you until they are parallel to the floor at a 90-degree angle. Pause at the top of the raise without swinging or using momentum, then lower your legs slowly back down to the starting vertical hang.

exercises.name: Cocoon Crunch
exercises.instructions_en: Lie flat on your back on an exercise mat with legs extended straight out and arms stretched overhead. Inhale and brace your abdominals. In a simultaneous movement, lift your shoulder blades and straight legs off the floor, curling your torso upward while pulling your knees into your chest and wrapping your arms around your shins, collapsing into a tight, compact cocoon ball. Squeeze your abdominals at peak contraction for a brief pause, then slowly release and extend your legs and arms back out straight until they hover an inch above the mat.

exercises.name: Decline Sit-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Secure your feet and ankles snugly beneath the padded rollers at the top of a decline abdominal bench, sitting with your torso upright. Cross your arms over your chest or place your hands lightly beside your ears. Inhale and slowly lower your torso backward down the decline bench, unrolling your spine under control until your back lightly touches the pad. Exhale and contract your abdominals, curling your torso upward through a complete range of motion until your body reaches a fully upright seated angle perpendicular to the bench. Squeeze your abs at the top, then lower slowly back down.

exercises.name: Forearm Plank Pike
exercises.instructions_en: Assume a standard forearm plank position with elbows directly under shoulders, forearms flat on the mat, and body in a rigid straight line from head to heels. Brace your core. Engaging your lower abdominals and hip flexors, lift your hips straight up toward the ceiling, rolling onto the tips of your toes to pull your pelvis upward into an inverted V-shape pike position. Keep your legs straight and forearms anchored firmly into the mat. Pause at peak hip elevation, then slowly lower your hips back down in a controlled line until you return to the flat forearm plank starting position.

exercises.name: Flutter Kicks
exercises.instructions_en: Lie flat on your back on a mat with legs fully extended and arms along your sides (or hands slightly under hips for lumbar support). Press your lower back firmly into the floor and brace your core. Lift both legs about 6 inches off the ground. Keeping legs straight with toes pointed, alternate kicking each leg up and down a few inches in a rapid, controlled flutter motion without letting heels touch the floor, maintaining steady breathing.

exercises.name: Scissor Kicks
exercises.instructions_en: Lie on your back with arms extended by your sides and lower back pressed into the mat. Raise your legs roughly 6 to 10 inches off the floor with knees straight. Spread your legs apart a couple of feet, then bring them back together, crossing your right ankle over your left ankle. Immediately open them wide again and bring them together, crossing the left ankle over the right. Continue this rhythmic horizontal criss-cross pattern smoothly while keeping your abs braced.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.instructions_en: Lie flat on your back with legs straight, toes pointed, and arms extended overhead alongside your ears. Press your lower back completely flat against the mat by engaging your abdominals and tilting your pelvis posteriorly. Simultaneously lift your shoulder blades, head, and straight legs 4 to 6 inches off the floor, creating a continuous curved, boat-like shape with your body. Hold this tension solidly with arms and legs locked out before gently releasing down.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.instructions_en: Start in a strong high plank with hands directly beneath your shoulders and feet slightly wider than hip-width apart to establish a stable base. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. Lift your right hand off the mat and tap your left shoulder, keeping your hips and torso completely square to the floor without rocking side-to-side. Place the right hand back down, then lift the left hand to tap the right shoulder before returning to the balanced plank.

exercises.name: Side Plank Hip Dips
exercises.instructions_en: Set up in a side plank on your right elbow, with forearm flat, elbow directly under shoulder, and feet stacked or staggered. Form a straight diagonal line from head to heels with left hand on your hip. Slowly lower your right hip toward the floor until it hovers an inch above the mat. Forcefully contract your right oblique and transverse abdominis to lift your hips back up, slightly higher than the starting line for a deep peak contraction, then lower again under control.

exercises.name: Commando Plank
exercises.instructions_en: Begin in a forearm plank with elbows directly under shoulders, core braced, and feet hip-width apart. Place your right hand flat on the floor where your right elbow was and press up, followed immediately by placing your left hand under the left shoulder to press into a full high plank. Reverse the movement by lowering your right elbow back to the floor, followed by the left elbow, returning to the forearm plank with minimal hip rotation.

exercises.name: Spiderman Plank
exercises.instructions_en: Start in a standard high plank or forearm plank position with body in a straight line. Lift your right foot off the floor and drive your right knee outward to the side and forward toward your right elbow, engaging your right oblique. Hold for a brief pause at the closest point of flexion, then extend the right leg back to the plank position. Repeat the movement on the left side, driving the left knee outward toward the left elbow before returning to start.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
exercises.instructions_en: Sit on a mat with your legs extended straight in front of you and hands placed on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing toward your feet. Press firmly through your palms and heels to lift your hips toward the ceiling. Raise until your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders, opening the chest and squeezing the glutes and hamstrings. Keep your neck neutral and gaze slightly upward. Hold the isometric peak contraction firmly before gently lowering your hips back down to touch the mat.

exercises.name: Bear Plank Hold
exercises.instructions_en:
Start on all fours with wrists stacked directly beneath shoulders and knees stacked directly beneath hips. Tuck your toes under, brace your abdominals, and press firmly through your palms to push the floor away. Lift both knees 1 to 2 inches off the mat so you are hovering on your hands and the balls of your feet. Maintain a flat, neutral back like a tabletop, with head and neck aligned. Hold this intense isometric core and quad contraction steadily before softly lowering your knees back to touch the mat.


=== Conditioning ===

exercises.name: Barbell Thruster
exercises.instructions_en: Hold a barbell in the front rack position resting across your clavicles and shoulders, with elbows pointing forward and feet shoulder-width apart. Inhale, brace your core, and descend smoothly into a full front squat until your hip crease is below the top of your knees with an upright torso. Explode upward through your heels, accelerating rapidly out of the squat. As your hips and knees reach full extension, transfer that upward momentum directly into your upper body, pressing the barbell smoothly overhead until your arms are fully locked out with the bar stacked over your head and heels. Lower the barbell smoothly back to your shoulders as you immediately cushion into the next squat descent.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Snatch
exercises.instructions_en: Place a dumbbell on the floor between your feet in a wide shoulder-width stance. Hinge at your hips and bend your knees with a flat back and proud chest, grasping the dumbbell with one hand in an overhand grip. Drive explosively through your heels and extend your hips, knees, and ankles simultaneously (triple extension), pulling the dumbbell vertically upward close along your body. As the dumbbell reaches chest level, rapidly drop your hips slightly to catch the weight overhead, punching your arm straight up to a crisp lockout with knees soft. Stand fully tall to complete the rep, then guide the dumbbell under control back to the floor.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
exercises.instructions_en: Place a kettlebell on the floor one foot in front of you. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hinge at the hips with a flat back, and grip the handle with one hand. Hike the kettlebell back between your thighs like a football snap. Explosively snap your hips forward to full vertical extension, driving the kettlebell upward in a high arc close to your body. As the bell floats near shoulder height, slide your hand smoothly around the handle to catch it softly against the back of your wrist, punching your arm straight overhead to a locked vertical position. Lower the kettlebell back down between your legs in a controlled pendulum arc.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
exercises.instructions_en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart with a kettlebell on the floor in front of you. Hinge at your hips, hike the kettlebell back between your legs, and snap your hips forward to clean the bell smoothly into the front rack at chest height with elbow tucked against your ribs. Settle in the rack for a split-second. Perform a quick, shallow knee dip of 2 to 3 inches with torso vertical, then explosively drive upward through your heels, launching the kettlebell overhead while dropping under the bell into a second shallow dip to catch it with arm fully locked out. Stand up tall to full extension, then lower the bell back to the rack and swing.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Lie flat on your back on a mat holding a kettlebell pressed vertically overhead in your right arm with elbow locked, right knee bent and foot flat on the floor, left arm and leg extended at 45 degrees. Keeping your eyes locked on the kettlebell and right arm rigidly vertical, roll up onto your left forearm, then press up onto your left palm. Drive through your right heel and left palm to bridge your hips high. Sweep your left leg back and place your left knee on the mat directly beneath your hip. Rotate your torso upright into a half-kneeling lunge position. Drive through your feet to stand tall with the kettlebell locked overhead, then carefully reverse each step to return to the floor.

exercises.name: Tire Flip
exercises.instructions_en: Stand facing a heavy tractor tire with feet placed wider than shoulder-width. Squat down deeply, pressing your chest firmly against the curved face of the tire with arms extended down to place your palms and fingers underneath the bottom tread. Keep your back flat and core braced. Drive forcefully upward and forward through your legs and hips, exploding out of the squat to launch the tire upward to approximately 45 degrees. Rapidly transition your hands from an underhand grip to an overhand push against the tread, driving forward forcefully with your arms and chest to push the tire completely over onto its opposite side, then reset your athletic stance.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a non-bouncing medicine ball with both hands at chest level. Inhale and raise the ball straight overhead, extending your hips, knees, and ankles onto the balls of your feet in full triple extension. In an explosive downward motion, engage your core and lats to forcefully throw and slam the medicine ball down into the floor directly in front of your feet, bending your knees and hinging your hips into an athletic squat. Catch the ball on its slight bounce or pick it up cleanly, returning smoothly to the overhead position.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides. Swing your arms backward while hinging at your hips and bending your knees into a loaded athletic quarter-squat. Explosively swing your arms forward and upward while driving forcefully off the floor with both feet, propelling your body horizontally forward through the air. Extend your hips fully in flight, then bring your knees forward and land softly on both feet simultaneously, absorbing the landing forces smoothly into an athletic quarter-squat with chest proud before standing upright.

exercises.name: Star Jump
exercises.instructions_en: Begin in a low crouch with feet together, knees deeply bent, torso inclined forward, and fingertips lightly touching near your ankles. In an explosive movement, jump straight up into the air as high as possible, simultaneously spreading your arms and legs wide diagonally outward so your entire body forms a large star or X-shape in mid-air at the apex of the jump. Quickly snap your arms and legs back together as you descend, landing softly and lightly on the balls of your feet to sink immediately back into the low crouch starting position.

exercises.name: Jumping Lunge
exercises.instructions_en: Start in a deep forward lunge with your right foot planted forward, left leg extended backward, and both knees bent at 90 degrees with your left knee hovering just an inch off the floor. Keep your torso upright and core braced. Drive explosively off the floor through both feet, jumping straight upward into the air. In mid-air, rapidly switch your legs in a scissor motion, driving your left leg forward and your right leg backward. Land softly and quietly, absorbing the impact directly into a deep lunge on the opposite side, then immediately repeat the scissor jump.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
exercises.instructions_en: Walk on a motorized fitness treadmill set to a steep incline (10 to 15 percent) at a steady, purposeful walking pace. Maintain an upright, tall posture with your chest lifted, shoulders back, and core lightly engaged. Avoid leaning excessively forward or clutching the handrails. Take rhythmic, deliberate strides, planting your front heel and rolling through the midfoot to drive off the toes, swinging your arms naturally and rhythmically at your sides in synchrony with your gait.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike
exercises.instructions_en: Sit upright on a stationary fitness exercise bike with the saddle adjusted to hip height so there is a slight, comfortable bend (roughly 25 to 30 degrees) in your knee at the bottom of the pedal stroke. Secure the balls of your feet into the pedal straps. Grasp the handlebars with a relaxed, neutral grip and keep your chest open with shoulders relaxed away from your ears. Pedal smoothly in continuous, fluid 360-degree circles, applying even pressure throughout both the downstroke and upstroke while maintaining a steady, rhythmic cadence.

exercises.name: Rope Climb
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall at the base of a heavy suspended climbing rope. Reach high overhead with both hands staggered along the rope in a firm overhand grip. Jump up slightly and clamp the rope securely between your feet using a J-hook or S-wrap foot wrap technique, locking the rope between your instep and opposite shoe sole. Stand up straight on your feet to extend your knees and hips, bearing your weight through your legs. Reach your hands higher one at a time, re-clamp your feet higher, and ascend smoothly before reversing your foot clamp and hand steps to descend under strict control.

exercises.name: Sprawl
exercises.instructions_en: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Drop your hips quickly, bend your knees, and place both hands flat on the floor inside your feet. Jump both feet back into a wide high plank position, momentarily dropping your hips slightly with core braced (without letting chest touch the floor). Immediately spring both feet back forward outside your hands into a low squat, lift your hands, and stand tall into your starting athletic ready position.

exercises.name: Plank Jacks
exercises.instructions_en: Start in a standard high plank with wrists directly beneath shoulders and feet together. Keep your core tight and back flat. Jump both feet outward to shoulder-width apart or wider, landing lightly on the balls of your feet, just like the leg motion of a jumping jack. Immediately jump both feet back together to the center, absorbing the impact softly without bouncing your hips up or letting your lower back sag.

exercises.name: Step Jacks
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides. Step your right foot wide out to the side while simultaneously raising both arms out to the sides and overhead until your hands meet. Tap the ball of your right foot on the floor, then step your right foot back to center as you lower your arms. Immediately repeat by stepping your left foot out wide and raising your arms overhead, maintaining a steady, low-impact rhythm.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing
exercises.instructions_en: Stand in an athletic boxing stance with left foot forward, right foot back, knees slightly bent, and fists held high guarding your chin. Extend your lead left arm straight forward in a quick, snappy jab, rotating the palm downward at full extension. Retract the left hand immediately back to your cheek while rotating your hips and rear right foot forward, throwing a powerful straight right cross. Snap the right hand back to the guard position, resetting the athletic stance.

exercises.name: Inchworm
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Hinge at your hips and bend forward, keeping legs as straight as comfortable, until your hands touch the floor. Walk your hands forward one at a time until your body forms a straight high plank position. Pause for a split-second with core braced, then walk your hands backward toward your feet, maintaining straight legs to stretch the hamstrings, and stand upright to the starting position.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Start in a standard high plank push-up position, then walk your feet forward toward your hands and elevate your hips high into the air, creating a sharp inverted V-shape with straight arms and legs. Shift your body weight forward onto your hands so your shoulders are stacked over your wrists. Inhale, bend your elbows backward at a 45-degree angle to your torso, and lower the crown of your head diagonally forward toward the floor until it lightly grazes the ground just ahead of your fingertips. Press forcefully through your palms and anterior deltoids to push back upward along the same diagonal path into the high pike starting position.

exercises.name: Handstand Push-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Kick up into a full vertical handstand against a flat wall, placing your hands shoulder-width apart approximately 6 to 8 inches from the wall, with fingers spread and core rigid. Begin with arms locked out completely, body straight, and heels lightly touching the wall. Slowly bend your elbows backward at a 45-degree angle, lowering your body under strict control until the top of your head gently touches an abmat or the floor. Press forcefully through your palms and shoulders, driving your body straight back up the wall until your arms are fully extended in the locked-out handstand starting position.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
exercises.instructions_en: Kick up into a solid handstand with your heels resting lightly against a sturdy wall (or walk up into a chest-to-wall handstand). Place your hands firmly on the floor shoulder-width apart, fingers gripping the mat. Lock your elbows out fully, press your shoulders actively upward toward your ears (scapular elevation), and brace your core and glutes to eliminate any excessive banana arch in your lower back. Hold this rock-solid, motionless isometric inverted handstand position steadily with calm breathing, then step your feet down smoothly under control.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Cuban Press
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall holding a pair of light dumbbells in front of your thighs with an overhand pronated grip, feet shoulder-width apart. Upright row the dumbbells vertically until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, forming a 90-degree angle at the elbows. Pausing with elbows high, externally rotate your shoulders upward 90 degrees until your forearms are vertical and dumbbells are beside your ears. From this goalpost position, press the dumbbells straight overhead to a full arm lockout. Reverse the movement smoothly: lower to goalpost, internally rotate to horizontal elbows, and lower to thighs.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Fly
exercises.instructions_en: Set the pulleys of a dual-cable crossover machine at upper chest/shoulder height without handles. Stand centered facing the machine. Grasp the left cable with your right hand and the right cable with your left hand so the cables cross in front of you. Take a step back to create tension, extending your arms straight forward at shoulder height with a soft micro-bend in your elbows. Keeping your arms in that horizontal plane, pull your hands outward and backward in a wide horizontal arc until your hands are level with your shoulders. Squeeze your rear deltoids hard, then slowly control the cables back to the starting crossed position.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Row
exercises.instructions_en: Attach a rope attachment to a cable pulley adjusted to chest or eye height. Grasp the rope ends with an overhand grip (thumbs pointing backward) and take two steps back into an athletic staggered stance with knees soft. Extend your arms forward to create cable tension with chest proud. Pull the rope ends directly toward your face and upper chest, flaring your elbows wide out to the sides at shoulder height. Squeeze your rear deltoids and pinch your shoulder blades together at the peak of the row, then slowly allow the cable to pull your arms back forward to full extension.

exercises.name: Band Y-Raise
exercises.instructions_en: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band handles with opposite hands so the band crosses in front of your shins. Begin with arms hanging down in front of your hips, thumbs pointing upward. Keeping your elbows straight with a soft micro-bend, raise both arms diagonally upward and outward at a 45-degree angle until your body forms a clean Y-shape overhead. Squeeze your lower trapezius and rear deltoids at the top of the range for a full second, then lower your arms slowly under control back to the crossed starting position.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Push Press
exercises.instructions_en: Clean a kettlebell into the front rack position resting on the outside of your forearm with elbow tucked against your ribs and feet shoulder-width apart. Keep your torso completely upright. Perform a quick, shallow knee dip of 2 to 3 inches, bending at the knees without hinging forward at the hips. Explosively drive through your heels to extend your knees and hips, using the momentum of your lower body to launch the kettlebell straight upward overhead to a full arm lockout. Stand tall at the top with glutes squeezed, then lower the bell smoothly back into the front rack cushion.

exercises.name: Machine Single-Arm Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions_en: Sit in a seated shoulder press machine, adjusting the seat height so the handles align at shoulder height. Grasp the right handle with an overhand or neutral grip while resting your left hand comfortably on your left thigh, feet planted flat on the floor. Keeping your torso strictly upright and core braced, press the right handle upward along the machine's guided track until your right arm is fully extended overhead. Pause for a moment to contract your shoulder at the top, then lower the handle smoothly and under control back to shoulder level.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Raise
exercises.instructions_en: Stand on the center of a resistance band with feet hip-width apart, holding the band handles at your sides with palms facing inward and arms hanging straight down. Keep your shoulders relaxed down and core braced. With a slight soft bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides in a wide arc until your upper arms are parallel to the floor at shoulder height, leading with your elbows and keeping your wrists neutral. Hold the peak contraction against the band's maximum tension for a full second, then lower your hands slowly back down to your sides.

exercises.name: Band Shoulder Press
exercises.instructions_en: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart on the center of a resistance band. Bring the band handles up to shoulder height, with palms facing forward, elbows tucked beneath your wrists, and the band running behind your arms. Inhale, brace your core, and press both handles straight up overhead against the increasing elastic tension until your arms are fully locked out overhead. Pause for a moment at peak extension with shoulders engaged, then lower your hands slowly under strict control back down to shoulder level.

exercises.name: Incline Rear Delt Raise
exercises.instructions_en: Set an adjustable gym bench to a 30 to 45-degree incline. Lie face-down prone on the bench with your chest supported against the pad and feet resting on the floor. Hold a pair of light dumbbells hanging vertically straight beneath your chest with palms facing each other and elbows slightly bent. Keeping that slight elbow bend fixed, raise the dumbbells outward and slightly backward in a wide semicircular arc until your upper arms are parallel to the floor, leading with your pinkies. Squeeze your posterior deltoids and rhomboids at the top, then lower slowly back to the starting hang.

exercises.name: Barbell Bradford Press
exercises.instructions_en:
Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart holding a barbell across your upper chest in a front rack position with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders. Inhale and press the barbell upward just enough to barely clear the top of your head. Without locking your elbows out overhead, rotate your shoulders to move the bar backward over the crown of your head and lower it under control to touch your upper trapezius behind your neck. Immediately reverse the movement, pressing the bar up just enough to clear your head and returning it smoothly back to the front rack.


=== Chest ===

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.instructions_en: Set both cable pulleys to their lowest position with single D-handles attached. Stand centered between the pulleys, grasp the handles with palms facing forward, and take one step forward into an athletic staggered stance with chest proud and shoulders retracted. Keeping your arms extended with a slight soft elbow bend, pull the cables upward and inward in a smooth diagonal arc until your hands meet directly in front of your upper chest/collarbone with pinkies slightly turned upward. Squeeze your upper chest intensely at the peak contraction for a full second, then slowly lower the cables back down to the starting stretch.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Fly
exercises.instructions_en: Sit upright in the pec deck machine with your back and head pressed firmly against the vertical support pad and feet flat on the floor. Adjust the seat height so that the handles or elbow pads align directly with the middle of your chest. Grasp the vertical handles with elbows slightly bent. Retract your shoulder blades and brace your core. Contract your pectorals to bring the handles together in a smooth, semicircular arc in front of your chest until they touch directly at your midline. Squeeze your inner and middle chest hard for a full second, then slowly reverse the motion back to the starting stretch position.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Barbell Bench Press
exercises.instructions_en: Lie flat on a standard bench press with your shoulder blades retracted and feet planted firmly on the floor. Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip spaced wide, approximately 1.5 to 1.75 times shoulder-width apart. Unrack the bar and hold it directly above your chest with arms locked. Inhale and lower the barbell slowly under control until it lightly touches your mid-chest, allowing your elbows to flare out at roughly 60 to 70 degrees from your torso while keeping forearms vertical. Press the barbell straight back up to full extension, driving through your palms and squeezing your chest at the top.

exercises.name: Svend Press
exercises.instructions_en: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart holding two light weight plates (or one plate) squeezed tightly together between the palms of your hands at the center of your chest, with fingers pointing forward and elbows flared out to the sides. Maintain continuous, maximum inward pressure against the plates with your palms throughout. Slowly press your hands straight out in front of your chest until your arms are fully extended at shoulder height, feeling an intense isometric contraction in your inner and middle pectorals. Hold for a full second, then slowly pull the plates back to your chest.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Set up in a push-up position with hands placed noticeably wider than shoulder-width apart (approximately 1.5 times shoulder width) and fingers pointing slightly outward. Keep glutes squeezed and core engaged. Lower your torso down until your chest is an inch above the floor, feeling an active stretch across the pectorals. Push powerfully through the palms to lockout at the top of the plank.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
exercises.instructions_en: Begin in an extra-wide push-up stance with hands turned slightly outward and feet hip-width apart. Lower your body down toward your right side, bending the right elbow while keeping the left arm completely straight and extended out to the side like an archer drawing a bow. Lower until your right chest hovers just over your right hand, then press back up through the right hand to the center starting position.

exercises.name: Hand-Release Push-Up
exercises.instructions_en:
Start in a rigid high plank position. Lower your body under control all the way to the floor until your chest, thighs, and pelvis rest flat. At the bottom, briefly lift both palms 2 inches off the floor to disengage momentum and ensure full depth. Plant your hands firmly back under your shoulders, brace your core, and push the floor away in one unified piece back to the top plank position.
